newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money skyrockets as banks balance books.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money skyrockets as banks balance books.

text.p: Dutch call money shot up on Monday as banks cleared their books at the end of the first half of the year, with some participants willing to pay as much as 4.5 percent, dealers said.
"Banks are clearing their books and call money rates are very volatile on this, but overnight money should regain its normal level of just over 3.00 percent tomorrow," said one.
"Somebody is buying everything they can get," said another dealer, adding it was only moderate portions of liquidity that were changing hands at 4.00 to 4.5 percent.
The dealer said the market was also somewhat short of liquidity due to an outflow of tax payments.

Call money rates started to bid at 3.125-3.25 percent in early trade, but later in the session prices started to fluctuate and some dealers ceased to quote on-screen prices in call money due to its extreme volatility.
Other rates were stable with three month deposits bid at an unchanged 3.12 percent.
The guilder was a little stronger at 112.55 per 100 marks from 112.575 on Friday.
